# Add Investor staff members

## Problem statement

The staff family has no member that manipulates the **market row** itself: every ability so far buffs income, reputation, costs, incidents or hand capacity. The Investor introduces a market-shaping role — one **free market re-roll per turn** that is **biased toward the business type where the Investor is employed** — giving players a reason to invest coins in scouting favourable offers rather than accepting the first row they see. Moving the Investor to a different business costs an action point, so the ability is a deliberate positioning decision rather than a free upgrade.

## Users

- **Main Street player (build planner)** — wants a market-manipulation tool that rewards placing an Investor next to the business type they are trying to grow.
- **Main Street player (mid-game)** — wants a coin-free way to dig for a missing synergy piece (e.g. a Food business while running a Food cluster).

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want a free market re-roll each turn while an Investor is employed, so that I can look for a better offer without paying the escalating re-roll cost (MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ).
- As a Main Street player, I want the Investor's free re-roll to be 75% likely to surface cards relevant to the business it is employed at, so that placing it near my cluster meaningfully improves my odds.
- As a Main Street player, I want to move the Investor to a different business for one action point, so that I can retarget the bias at a cost.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Investor card exists in the catalog.** A new `staff-investor` row is added to `src/card-data.csv` (feature flag `freeMarketRerollPerTurn`, bias `0.75`, no hand slots, generalist `allowedBusinessTypes`), with a tier assignment, cost, ongoing cost and description consistent with the staff ladder and the ×100 coin scale; it flows into the general market via the existing tier-gated staff deck (`createStaffDeck`).
- **AC2 — One free re-roll per turn.** While at least one Investor is employed, the player may perform **one** coin-free, action-free market re-roll per week/turn (no coin deduction, no action spent); multiple Investors do not stack (still one per turn). The free re-roll is gated by a per-turn flag reset at `WeekStart` alongside `peekUsedThisTurn`/`favourUsedThisTurn`, and it **advances the per-turn escalation counter** (`marketRefreshesThisTurn`, `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`) so the next paid re-roll costs the escalated price. Once used, further re-rolls fall back to the normal paid path.
- **AC3 — Relevance bias.** On the Investor's free re-roll, each drawn slot has a **75% chance** to be drawn from the "relevant" pool for the business the Investor is employed at, falling back to the fully random pool when the relevant pool is exhausted; the remaining probability is entirely random. Relevance is defined as a shared synergy type (business/community-space `synergyTypes`; event `targetSynergy`/effect; staff `allowedBusinessTypes` overlap with the hosting business's synergy types) — the free `refillSingleRowMarket` path is parameterised so the normal `refreshMarket`/`cycleMarketCards` paths stay fully random.
- **AC4 — All staff relocation costs an action point.** Relocating a hired staff member from one business to another is exposed as a player action and consumes **1 action point** for **all** staff (the existing `placeStaffOnBusiness` placement is action-free today and must be action-gated when used as a relocation; the initial placement at hire time remains part of the hire action). The move respects `allowedBusinessTypes` and employment-slot capacity, is undoable, and is persisted.
- **AC5 — UI & tooltips.** The market re-roll button/tooltip and the Investor's staff tooltip/employed-staff summary surface (a) whether the free re-roll is still available this turn and (b) the 75% relevance bias; the button label/tooltip reflect the coin-free state when available and the escalated cost when not. Wording stays consistent with the `MS-0MTIS895Y008XGQ1` "Research" rename if that lands first.
- **AC6 — Undo, save/load and determinism.** The per-turn free-re-roll flag, the per-turn escalation counter it increments (`marketRefreshesThisTurn`), the Investor's location and any bias state participate in undo/redo (`snapshotAction`) and in `MainStreetStateSerialize` (serialize + migrate backfill + deserialize), so mid-turn reload preserves both availability and the escalated next price; the bias draw uses the seeded RNG (`state.rng`) so same-seed ⇒ same-game determinism holds.
- **AC7 — Tests.** Unit/integration tests cover: catalog + CSV contract; free re-roll is coin-free, once per turn, resets at `WeekStart` and advances the escalation counter; the 75% relevance bias (deterministic with a seeded RNG) and its random fallback; movement action cost + undo + save/load round-trip; and existing re-roll/discount/action-economy tests are updated for the new card and counts.
- **AC8 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README.md`, the Main Street rules docs (`core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `content-design-and-progression.md`, `card-catalog.md`) and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- **AC9 — Quality gate.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **New mechanic, not just data.** The relevance bias and the free re-roll are new engine behaviour; they must be additive and must not change existing behaviour when no Investor is employed.
- **Single source of truth for re-roll cost.** The free re-roll must not silently bypass `refreshMarketCost()`; the paid path and its escalation (`MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`) remain authoritative for non-free re-rolls, and the free re-roll must increment the same per-turn escalation counter.
- **Reuse the market composition model.** `refillSingleRowMarket` (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts`) enforces the ≥1-business row composition; the biased draw must preserve that invariant.
- **Placement/employment invariant.** `business.employedStaff` and `staff.employedAtSlot` are kept in sync by the existing placement helpers; the move action must route through them.
- **Art drift guard.** `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` requires every unique card name to map to dedicated art or a documented pending-art target, and forbids growing the art-less baseline (currently 79). The Investor therefore needs a dedicated 1024×1024 sprite **or** an explicit, producer-approved pending-art entry (see `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E`).
- **Coin scale.** All coin values are ×100 (per the integer-economy migration); the Investor's cost/ongoing cost must follow the existing staff ladder (`MS-0MULWBSF9000Z64Z`).

## Existing state

- **No Investor exists** anywhere in the repo or worklog (searched `investor`, case-insensitive, excluding `node_modules`/`dist`); only the unrelated `Investor Bonanza` event fixture appears in a test.
- **Market re-roll is already action-free** (`core-rules-and-mechanics.md` §6.0 "Free operations: Market re-roll/refresh"), so "without using an action" means the Investor's re-roll is free of **coins** as well; the normal re-roll costs `REFRESH_MARKET_COST` (500, escalating per `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`).
- `refillSingleRowMarket(state)` (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts:162`) builds the row: 3 slots, ≥1 business, at most 1 upgrade / 1 event / 1 staff, drawing via `state.rng` (seeded).
- `refreshMarket(state)` / `refreshMarketCost(state)` / `canRefreshMarket(state)` live in `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`; discounts come from `refreshCostDiscount` staff and the Negotiator skill.
- **Staff placement is free today**: `placeStaffOnBusiness` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:880`) explicitly consumes no action/coins; `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand`/`removeStaffFromBusinessCommand` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts:674/692`) wrap it in `snapshotAction`. There is currently **no** player-facing "move staff" action.
- Staff card fields live in `StaffCard` (`src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts:330`), parsed in `MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` (CSV columns incl. `actionsPerTurn`, `peekOncePerTurn`, `allowedBusinessTypes`); the catalog currently holds **25** staff rows.
- Per-turn gates (`peekUsedThisTurn`, `favourUsedThisTurn`, `businessPlacedThisTurn`) are reset in `executeWeekStart` (`src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts`).
- Card-count baselines that will shift when a staff row is added: `tests/main-street/group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts` (`toHaveLength(25)`), `tests/main-street/meta-progression.test.ts` (166 / 174 totals), `docs/main-street/card-catalog-baseline.json`, `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json`.

## Desired change

- **CSV/catalog:** add `staff-investor` with a new bias column (e.g. `marketRelevanceBias = 0.75`) plus a free-re-roll marker (e.g. `freeMarketRerollPerTurn`), no `handSlotsAdded`, generalist `allowedBusinessTypes`, and a description in the existing "reduces X by Y" house style.
- **Types/parsing:** add the new optional `StaffCard` fields and parse them in `MainStreetCardsTemplates` (numeric column for the bias; boolean/flag column for the ability).
- **Engine:** add `investorFreeRerollUsedThisTurn` state (reset at `WeekStart`), a `canUseFreeMarketReroll`/`useFreeMarketReroll` pair (coin-free, action-free, once per turn) that **increments `marketRefreshesThisTurn`**, and a `refillSingleRowMarket`-compatible biased draw parameterised by the hosting business's synergy types + `0.75`.
- **Movement:** add a move-staff engine function + command that charges 1 action via the existing weekly action budget for **any** staff relocation, reusing `placeStaffOnBusiness` semantics (adding the action gate at the command layer).
- **Serialization:** add the new state field to serialize, migrate (backfill `false`/`0`) and deserialize.
- **UI:** market re-roll button/tooltip shows the free re-roll availability; staff tooltip/employed-staff summary states the free re-roll + 75% bias; a move-staff affordance that costs an action.
- **Docs & art:** update the rules/catalog/progression docs; add the Investor sprite (or a documented pending-art entry) and regenerate `card-art-map.json`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — new `staff-investor` row (new bias column + free-re-roll flag; tier, cost, ongoing cost, description).
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — `StaffCard.freeMarketRerollPerTurn?` / `StaffCard.marketRelevanceBias?` (+ doc comments).
- `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — parse the new CSV columns into the new fields.
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — free re-roll path (`canUseFreeMarketReroll` / `useFreeMarketReroll`), bias-aware `refreshMarket` variant, and cost/label reporting.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — parameterise `refillSingleRowMarket` with an optional relevance pool; keep the default path unchanged.
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` — reset the per-turn free-re-roll flag.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — new per-turn state field (and serialized-state entry).
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — serialize, migrate backfill (and deserialize) the new field.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` / `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — move-staff engine function + command (1 action), free-re-roll command.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` / `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — helpers to detect the employed Investor and its hosting business synergy types.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — free-re-roll button state, tooltip and availability text.
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — employed-staff summary / staff tooltip line for the new ability.
- `src/card-art-map.json`, `src/sprites/`, `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` — Investor art (or a documented pending-art entry).
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — free re-roll, relevance bias, movement cost.
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` — staff table row + ability cell.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — staff catalogue row.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog-baseline.json`, `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json` — catalog baselines.
- `tests/main-street/` — new `investor-staff.test.ts` (free re-roll, bias, movement) plus updates to `refresh-market.test.ts`, `group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts`, `meta-progression.test.ts`, `staff-business-type-matching.test.ts`, `card-art.test.ts`, `hud-tooltips.test.ts`, `action-economy.test.ts` and any staff-count assertions.

## Related work

See **Related work (automated report)** below, plus manually identified items:

- `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ` — "Reroll to cost more" (open): escalates the paid re-roll cost; its appendix explicitly leaves "free re-rolls do not advance the escalation counter" as an assumption to settle with this item.
- `MS-0MTIS895Y008XGQ1` — "Rename the reroll button 'Research'" (in-progress): touches the same market re-roll button/tooltip; coordinate wording and the free-re-roll affordance.
- `MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0` — "Some staff cards should add action points" (completed): establishes the weekly action budget and the staff card UI/action patterns the movement cost builds on.
- `MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M` — "Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects" (completed): most recent end-to-end staff-ability implementation (CSV → engine → docs → tests); follow its structure.
- `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E` — "Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card" (open): owns the art-less baseline; the Investor raises the drift-guard question.
- `MS-0MUAYBAHW007RMSL` — "Add a charity shop" (completed): precedent for adding a card and updating the catalog/count baselines.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Decision (free = coins-free, escalation-advancing):** because market re-roll is already action-free, "free re-roll, without using an action" means **no coin cost and no action cost**, but the free re-roll **advances** the per-turn escalation counter. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (bias definition):** "relevant to the type of business they are currently located at" = shares a synergy type with the hosting business; businesses/community-space by `synergyTypes`, events by `targetSynergy`, staff by `allowedBusinessTypes` overlap. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (bias application):** the 75% applies per drawn slot with a random fallback; the entire row is not a single 75% roll. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (no stacking):** multiple Investors still grant a single free re-roll per turn (avoids a degenerate multi-Investor loop). *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (movement scope):** **all** staff relocation costs an action; the initial placement at hire time is unchanged. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Risk (scope creep / existing behaviour):** the re-roll cost item and the rename item touch the same button; implementing the free re-roll without advancing the counter would desynchronise the displayed price, and newly action-gating **all** staff relocation changes an existing free operation (and its tests). Mitigation: keep `refreshMarketCost()` authoritative, increment the shared counter on the free re-roll, and update the staff-placement tests in the same change.
- **Risk (determinism/tests):** adding a card changes seeded deck draws and several fixed-count baselines; many fixtures inline counts. Mitigation: update the documented baselines and count assertions in the same change, and cover the bias with a seeded-RNG test.
- **Risk (art drift guard):** a new art-less card fails `card-art.test.ts`; either supply a sprite or get a producer-approved pending-art entry, otherwise the item is blocked by `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E`.
- **Risk (save compat):** forgetting the migrate backfill leaves old saves with `undefined` and a throwing/NaN free-re-roll gate. Mitigation: backfill in `migrateSerializedState` and assert a round-trip.
- **Risk (balance):** a free re-roll per turn plus a 75% biased row is a strong information advantage; cost/tier may need balancing (`balancing-methodology.md`). Mitigation: pick a mid/premium tier and revisit after playtest.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Round 1 (route: herdr auto-dispatch, 2026-09-30; answered by the producer 2026-09-30).**

- **Q1 (free re-roll semantics):** "The market re-roll is already action-free, so what does the Investor's 'free re-roll' free you from, and does it stack/interact with the escalating cost (`MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`)? Options: (a) one **coin-free** re-roll per turn, does **not** advance the escalation counter, multiple Investors do **not** stack; (b) one coin-free re-roll per Investor (stacks); (c) the free re-roll also resets the escalation counter; (d) freeform."
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-30):** one coin-free, action-free re-roll per turn; it **does advance the escalation counter**; multiple Investors do **not** stack.

- **Q2 (relevance definition & application):** "How is 'relevant to the type of business they are currently located at' defined, and how does the 75% apply? Options: (a) a shared synergy type (business/community-space `synergyTypes`, event `targetSynergy`, staff `allowedBusinessTypes` overlap), applied **per drawn slot** with random fallback; (b) relevant by exact business name only; (c) the **whole row** is 75% likely to be relevant; (d) freeform."
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-30):** as recommended — **(a)** shared synergy type, applied per drawn slot, with random fallback.

- **Q3 (movement cost & scope):** "Staff placement is action-free today. Should the Investor's move cost an action point, and does that apply to all staff? Options: (a) **Investor only** pays 1 action to relocate; other staff stay free; (b) **all staff** relocation costs 1 action; (c) the move is free but limited to once per turn; (d) freeform."
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-30):** **(b)** — **all** staff relocation costs 1 action.

**Secondary assumptions (not asked in Round 1, to keep to the ≤3-question limit):**

- **Card economics (default):** `staff-investor` is a generalist (all synergy types), `handSlotsAdded: 0`, tier 5, cost 1000, ongoing 125 — mirroring the tier-5 specialist band (Financial Advisor). *Recorded as an assumption; the producer may re-balance.*
- **Art (default):** add a dedicated 1024×1024 Investor sprite and regenerate `card-art-map.json`; if art cannot be produced, request a producer-approved pending-art entry so the drift guard passes.
- **Rename coordination (default):** implement the free-re-roll affordance on the existing re-roll button so it survives the `MS-0MTIS895Y008XGQ1` "Research" rename without conflicting wording.

**Research finding (agent, 2026-09-30):** The free re-roll and relevance bias are **not** implemented anywhere (repo + worklog search). The re-roll is already action-free and coin-costed (`src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`); `refillSingleRowMarket` (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts:162`) is the single composition point; staff placement is action-free (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:880`). This item is therefore a **new mechanic + card + docs + art** change, not a data-only change.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E** – Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card (1024×1024 source; eliminate generic Fallback art) (open)
- **MS-0MTIIL6J200291ZQ** – Per-owner income routing; shared event/incident resolution (open)
- **MS-0MUE2U21C0007BKL** – [test-failure] upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts > animates the transfer from the drop location and plays the upgrade SFX (beginDrag timeout) — failing test (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: ability, ac4, ac5, acceptance, action (+430 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: abilities, ability, acceptance, action, add (+332 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: ability, acceptance, action, add, added (+310 more)

# Intake Brief: Render the storyline graph (Mermaid to SVG) in the docs build (MS-0MUNB54KU005084C)

**Priority: High** | **Type: Chore** | **Assignee: Map**

> Discovered from the "write storylines" epic (`MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV`), C6
> documentation roadmap. The epic commits a generated Mermaid flowchart at
> `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd`; this item renders it to a portable
> image so the graph is viewable without a Mermaid-aware renderer and links it
> from the canonical storyline doc.

## Problem statement

The storyline graph is committed only as a Mermaid source file
(`docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd`). Anyone reading the repository on a
plain Markdown viewer, on GitHub without Mermaid support, or in a rendered docs
artefact cannot see the graph and cannot easily tell the shape of the shipped
storylines. Rendering it to a portable SVG in a documented docs step and
linking it from `docs/main-street/storylines.md` makes the graph viewable
everywhere, without requiring a Mermaid-aware renderer.

## Users

- **Content designers / producers** — need to see the storyline shape at a
  glance in the docs, without installing Mermaid tooling.
  - *"As a content designer, I want the storyline graph shown as an image in the
    docs, so I can inspect the shipped chains without a Mermaid renderer."*
- **Developers / reviewers** — need the rendered graph to stay in sync with the
  committed Mermaid source so reviews trust the picture.
  - *"As a reviewer, I want a drift guard between the rendered image and the
    committed `.mmd`, so a stale graph cannot be merged."*
- **Docs build / maintainers** — need a deterministic, reproducible render step
  with no manual copy-paste.
  - *"As a maintainer, I want one documented command that regenerates the
    rendered graph, so the artefact is reproducible."*

## Acceptance Criteria

> **Finalised** per producer answers to Q1–Q3 (2026-10-07): minimal npm render
> step (A); reuse Playwright + `mermaid` devDependency (B); SVG-vs-`.mmd` drift
> guard (A).

1. **Rendered artefact** — a rendered graph image (`docs/main-street/storyline-graph.svg`)
   is committed under `docs/main-street/` and is viewable without a
   Mermaid-aware renderer (SVG preferred; PNG only if SVG cannot be emitted).
2. **Reproducible render step** — a documented npm script renders the committed
   `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` into the committed image
   deterministically (no RNG, timestamp or wall-clock input; byte-identical on
   re-run). The renderer is a **devDependency only** and does not enter the
   game bundle.
3. **Doc link** — `docs/main-street/storylines.md` embeds or links the rendered
   image (in §7.2 "The shipped graph" and/or §11 "Related documents"),
   documenting the new regeneration command in the §5 tooling table.
4. **Drift guard (validation)** — an automated test/check fails when the
   committed rendered SVG drifts from the committed `.mmd`. The existing
   `.mmd`-vs-`src/card-data.csv` `--check` guard must continue to pass.
5. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No mandatory new runtime dependency for the game** — any renderer
  dependency is a **devDependency** only and must not enter the game bundle.
  Reuse the already-installed `playwright` Chromium (no second Chromium
  download).
- **Determinism** — the render must be reproducible from the committed `.mmd`;
  no timestamps/ids embedded in the output that would churn on every run.
- **Mermaid is the source of truth** — the `.mmd` remains the generated
  artefact of record; the image is derived, never hand-edited.
- **Licensing** — any added dependency must be permissively licensed (MIT,
  Apache-2.0, CC0). The `mermaid` package is MIT.
- **Scope** — do not redesign the graph content or the storyline model, and do
  not build a full static docs site (deferred to `MS-0MUYK064P0032374`). This
  item only renders and links the existing graph.

## Existing state (repo research)

- `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` — committed 98-line Mermaid flowchart;
  choice cards as diamonds, plain incidents as rounded rectangles, cycle edges
  as `==>`.
- `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` — generator/CLI: `--format mermaid|json`,
  `--out`, `--check` (drift guard). Deterministic (sorted ids, no RNG/clock).
- `src/scripts/storyline-graph-cli.ts` — CLI entry; npm script
  `storylines:graph` (`vite-node src/scripts/storyline-graph-cli.ts`).
- `tests/main-street/storyline-graph.test.ts` — asserts the committed `.mmd`
  matches regeneration from `src/card-data.csv` (existing drift guard).
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — canonical doc. §5 Tooling, §7.2 shipped
  graph, §10 Roadmap (links this work item), §11 Related documents (links the
  `.mmd`).
- `package.json` — scripts include `storylines:graph`, `validate:storylines`;
  devDependencies already include `playwright`, `sharp`, `vite-node`/`vite`,
  `vitest`. **No `mermaid`, `@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli`, `puppeteer` or docs site
  generator (mkdocs/docusaurus) is present anywhere in the repo or `core/`.**
- **There is no "docs build"** in `tce-main-street`: `docs/` is plain Markdown,
  there is no docs npm script, no mkdocs/docusaurus config, and no docs-site CI
  workflow. The only Pages workflow (`core/.github/workflows/deploy.yml`)
  deploys the game bundle, not these docs.

## Desired change

1. **Render** the committed `.mmd` into a portable SVG via a documented,
   deterministic script/npm command that reuses the installed Playwright
   Chromium and the `mermaid` JS package (devDependency).
2. **Commit** the rendered SVG under `docs/main-street/`.
3. **Link/embed** the rendered SVG from `docs/main-street/storylines.md` and
   update the §5 tooling table and §10 roadmap row.
4. **Guard** the rendered SVG against drift from the `.mmd` with a test/check;
   document the regeneration workflow.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.svg` — **new** rendered artefact.
- `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` — input (unchanged source of truth).
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — add image embed/link; update §5 tooling,
  §7.2 shipped graph, §10 roadmap.
- `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` — possibly extend with an `svg`/render
  format or a separate renderer module.
- `src/scripts/render-storyline-graph.ts` — **new** render script (if separate
  from the existing CLI).
- `package.json` — new npm script (e.g. `storylines:graph:svg`) and the
  `mermaid` devDependency.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-graph.test.ts` (or a new test) — rendered-image
  drift guard.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV** — "write storylines" epic (completed/in review); this
  item is roadmap item C6-deferred.
- **MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0** — "Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema"
  (completed) — produced `storyline-graph.mmd`, the JSON manifest, and the
  existing `.mmd` drift test this item builds on.
- **MS-0MUMP968H005MXZY** — "Canonical docs, cross-references & doc-drift
  guard" (completed) — owns `docs/main-street/storylines.md` §10 Roadmap and §11
  Related documents.
- **MS-0MUYK064P0032374** — **new**: "Static docs site that renders Mermaid docs
  at build time" (medium, discovered-from this item) — the deferred option (B)
  from Q1.
- **MS-0MUNC8AOL0092BE5** — "Fix stale example-games/main-street paths in docs
  after the src/ migration" (open) — touches the same docs tree; coordinate if
  both touch `storylines.md`.
- **MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9** / **MS-0MUNB5D7K001GH19** — sibling deferred
  storyline roadmap items (conditional options; visual authoring editor).
- **MS-0MUSY1M1F003IS47** — "Editor host & read-only graph viewer" (blocked) —
  the viewer may consume the rendered graph.

### Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0** – Some staff cards should add action points (completed)
- **MS-0MUSY1M1F003IS47** – Editor host & read-only graph viewer (blocked)
- **MS-0MUMP93DI0018OGV** – Storyline model & extraction seam (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: add, already, aware, build, card (+30 more)
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — matched: add, already, build, card, check (+28 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: add, already, aware, build, card (+24 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **No docs build exists (MEDIUM).** The premise "in the docs build" has no
  counterpart in the repo. *Mitigation:* Q1 answer (A) creates a minimal render
  step; the full docs-site build is deferred to `MS-0MUYK064P0032374`.
- **Determinism / review churn (MEDIUM).** SVG output can embed ids/timestamps.
  *Mitigation:* assert byte-stable output in a test; pin the `mermaid` version.
- **Headless renderer flakiness in CI (MEDIUM).** Playwright Chromium must be
  available in the test environment. *Mitigation:* reuse the already-installed
  Playwright; keep the render a dev-only npm script and guard it in tests.
- **Drift staleness (LOW).** A committed image can silently diverge from the
  `.mmd`. *Mitigation:* AC4 SVG-vs-`.mmd` drift guard.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Requests to redesign the graph layout, add legends, or
  build a full docs site must be recorded as separate work items, not absorbed
  here (the docs-site request is already tracked as `MS-0MUYK064P0032374`).
- **Assumption** — SVG is the preferred format (scalable, text-searchable);
  PNG is acceptable only if the chosen renderer cannot emit SVG.
- **Assumption** — the `.mmd` stays the generated source of truth; the image is
  derived.
- **Assumption** — CHANGELOG is managed by the release pipeline and is out of
  scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

> **Status: answered.** Producer answers received 2026-10-07 (this session).
> Recommendations were advisory; the producer's choices are recorded below.

- **Q1 — Delivery surface ("the docs build").** *There is no docs build in
  `tce-main-street` (docs are plain Markdown; no mkdocs/docusaurus/Pages
  pipeline). How should the rendered graph be delivered?*
  Options:
  - **(A) Add a minimal render step** — a new npm script that renders
    `storyline-graph.mmd` → `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.svg`, with the SVG
    committed and regenerated like the `.mmd`.
  - **(B) Create a full static docs build** (mkdocs/docusaurus/Pages) that
    renders Mermaid at build time — larger scope, new toolchain.
  - **(C) Commit a one-off rendered SVG** with no build/pipeline; document
    manual regeneration only.
  - **Recommended: (A)** — smallest change that makes the graph viewable
    everywhere and keeps it reproducible, without adopting a docs-site
    toolchain the repo does not otherwise use.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-07): (A)** — minimal npm render step.
    **Follow-up:** option (B) tracked separately as
    `MS-0MUYK064P0032374` (medium priority). Source: interactive reply.

- **Q2 — Renderer / dependency policy.** *Rendering Mermaid requires a renderer;
  none is installed, and the epic constrained new runtime deps. Which renderer?*
  Options:
  - **(A) Add `@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli` (`mmdc`) as a devDependency** —
    bundles a Puppeteer/Chromium download; heaviest.
  - **(B) Reuse the already-installed `playwright` Chromium** and add the
    `mermaid` JS package as a devDependency, rendering headlessly.
  - **(C) No build-time renderer** — author/commit the SVG manually; guard
    drift only lightly.
  - **Recommended: (B)** — Playwright is already a devDependency (no second
    Chromium download) and keeps the renderer dev-only; the `mermaid` package
    is permissively licensed (MIT).
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-07): (B)** — reuse the already-installed
    Playwright Chromium and add the `mermaid` JS package as a devDependency
    (headless render). Source: interactive reply.

- **Q3 — Drift gate scope.** *Should the new step also fail when the rendered
  SVG drifts from the `.mmd`?*
  Options:
  - **(A) Yes** — add an SVG-vs-`.mmd` drift guard (test/script), in addition
    to the existing `.mmd`-vs-CSV guard.
  - **(B) No** — render the SVG but do not gate on it.
  - **Recommended: (A)** — a stale rendered graph is exactly the failure this
    item is meant to prevent.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-07): (A)** — add an SVG-vs-`.mmd` drift guard
    on top of the existing `.mmd`-vs-CSV guard. Source: interactive reply.

---

## Reopened scope: per-storyline rendering (2026-10-08)

> **Producer review.** The combined SVG is unreadable: 71 nodes but only 11
> connected (the 5 storyline chains). Mermaid lays the 60 isolated
> (non-storyline) incidents out in a single horizontal row, producing a
> 13,268px-wide strip of tiny boxes. The producer asked to break the graph into
> pages, one parent box per page, with the standalone incidents shown as a
> compact index/table (option C). This is a **rendering/layout change only** —
> the storyline model and the committed `.mmd` source of truth are unchanged.

### Added Acceptance Criteria

7. **Per-storyline pages** — the render step emits one SVG per storyline parent
   (five: tax, health, economy, labor, restaurant), each showing only that
   storyline's chain at a readable size, committed under `docs/main-street/`.
   *Metric: five committed `storyline-graph-<slug>.svg` files; each renders the
   storyline's node/edge subset.*
8. **Standalone-incident index** — the 60 non-storyline incidents are
   represented as a compact index/table (not boxes) and are drift-guarded
   against the manifest. *Metric: index present in `storylines.md` and a test
   regenerates/comparses it from the manifest.*
9. **Docs, guards and tests updated** — `storylines.md` §7.2 embeds the
   per-storyline gallery and the index table; the render `--check` guard and
   the render tests cover every page; the existing `.mmd`-vs-CSV guard stays
   green; the full suite passes. *Metric: full suite green; `--check` exits 0.*

### Design decisions (assumptions recorded)

- One page = one **storyline** (the parent/root incident and its chain), not one
  page per choice card. This keeps the tax cycle (3 cards) together.
- "Compact index/table" is implemented as a generated Markdown table in the
  canonical doc (the natural index for plain Markdown docs), not as boxes.
- The combined `storyline-graph.mmd` remains the generated source of truth; the
  monolithic combined SVG is replaced by the per-storyline pages.

---

## Reopened scope: per-event detail tables (2026-10-08)

> **Producer review.** The per-storyline diagrams show only the event names.
> The producer asked for much more information about each event in a storyline:
> the descriptive text, the impact on game state, and anything else critical.
> Presentation chosen: a **detail table below each diagram** (option A).

### Added Acceptance Criteria

10. **Event detail data** — the storyline manifest exposes, for every event,
    its descriptive text (`effect`), `trigger`, `tier`, `cost`,
    `target`/`targetSynergy`, `coinDelta`/`reputationDelta`/`coinPercentDelta`,
    `duration`/`effectType`/`multiplier`, and the per-option `effectPolicy`;
    the JSON schema is extended and the schema drift test stays green.
    *Metric: manifest node/edge fields present; schema validation passes.*
11. **Per-event detail tables** — a generated detail table (one row per event:
    description, normalised game-state impact, choice routing) is rendered below
    each per-storyline diagram in `storylines.md` §7.2. *Metric: tables present
    and readable.*
12. **Drift guard + docs + full suite** — the detail tables are drift-guarded
    against the manifest (`npm run storylines:graph:svg -- --check` and a test);
    the docs are updated; the full suite passes. *Metric: `--check` exits 0;
    full suite green.*

### Design decisions (assumptions recorded)

- The tables are generated between `<!-- BEGIN/END GENERATED -->` markers in
  `storylines.md`; the render step splices only the marked regions, so hand-
  written prose is never clobbered.
- Table rows lead with the event **name** (with the id) and use four columns so
  they do not collide with the §7.2 chains-table parser in the doc-drift test.
- `tier` comes from the exported `CARD_TIER_MAP`; duration fields are read from
  the `DurationEventCard` variant.

---

## Reopened scope: per-storyline docs, assets folder, richer boxes (2026-10-08)

> **Producer review.** The detail tables added the information but the doc is
> still not readable: `storylines.md` is now long, and the diagram boxes show
> only the name/id. Producer requirements: separate each storyline's `.md` from
> `storylines.md`; move the SVGs into an assets folder; and put a brief
> description + game-state impact inside each box.

### Added Acceptance Criteria

13. **Per-storyline documents** — each storyline has its own committed Markdown
    document (`docs/main-street/storylines/<slug>.md`) containing its diagram
    and per-event detail table; `storylines.md` links to them and no longer
    embeds the diagrams/tables. *Metric: 5 per-storyline docs; `storylines.md`
    contains links, not embeds.*
14. **Assets folder** — the rendered SVGs live under
    `docs/main-street/assets/` (`storyline-graph-<slug>.svg`) and every
    reference (docs, tests, guards) uses the new path. *Metric: no committed
    SVG remains at the old path; links resolve.*
15. **Readable boxes** — each diagram box shows a brief form of the event's
    description and its game-state impact (not just name/id). *Metric: rendered
    SVG node labels contain the brief text and impact; drift guard updated.*

### Design decisions (assumptions recorded)

- "Brief form of the description" = the first sentence of the card's `effect`
  text, truncated to a bounded length.
- "Game-state impact" = the normalised impact already computed for the detail
  tables (coin/reputation deltas, proportional coin loss, duration multiplier).
- Assets live at `docs/main-street/assets/` (no existing docs-asset convention;
  `screenshots/` is unrelated and specific to screenshots).
- The per-storyline docs are generated (like the incident index) and
  drift-guarded, so the tables/diagrams never drift from the manifest.

Discovered from MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4 (Level-2 upgrade prerequisite gate blocks expensive-tier adoption in greedy Monte Carlo).

## Goal

Make the four level-2 capstone upgrades reachable in the canonical greedy Monte Carlo profile by changing **upgrade-deck composition / market weighting**, not card stats.

## Why (evidence from MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4)

Card-data-only cost tuning (level-1 prerequisites 700→400/900→500; level-2 900/1400/1400/1400→700/1000/1000/1000) left the four capstones at ~0–2.8% M1 on greedy/Medium/200 seeds. An even more aggressive variant (level-1 cost 200, level-2 cost 400) produced **identical** adoption, proving cost/affordability is not the binding constraint.

The binding constraint is co-occurrence: a capstone can only be bought when a parent business is already at level 1 AND the capstone card is in the market — but the market shows at most **one upgrade per turn** drawn from a 78-card upgrade deck (39 templates × 2 copies). Across 200 runs only 0–1 runs had both a level-1 parent and the matching capstone on offer.

## Proposed levers (pick one, measure with before/after Monte Carlo)

1. Increase the upgrade-deck copies for the four capstone templates (e.g. 2 → 4) and/or their level-1 prerequisite branches.
2. Add a per-card market weight / draw-weight column so chain cards appear more often than generic upgrades.
3. Reserve one market upgrade slot for chain-relevant upgrades when a matching parent exists at the required level.

Any option must preserve US-19 (`requiredLevel: 1`, `canPurchaseUpgrade()` level equality), the Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard ladder, and the ±0.05 Medium win-rate band.

## Acceptance criteria

1. All four level-2 capstones (upg-grand-bakehouse, upg-restaurant, upg-multiplex, upg-luxury-retreat) reach **≥5% M1** on the canonical greedy/Medium profile (200 seeds, prefix mc-balance, 60 turns), with before/after evidence commit-stamped.
2. Level-1 prerequisite adoption measurably rises vs the MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4 after-state.
3. US-19 level gate and two-step chain preserved; no card-stat-only change.
4. Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard ladder preserved; Medium win-rate within ±0.05 of the pre-change baseline.
5. Tests cover the new deck/weight rule; full suite green.

## Key files (predicted)

- src/MainStreetCardsDecks.ts (createUpgradeDeck copies / weights)
- src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts / MainStreetStateSetup.ts (market draw)
- src/card-data.csv (only if a weight column is added)
- tests/main-street/level2-upgrade-chain.test.ts (extend)

## References

- MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4 — source item (card-data tuning attempted; ≤2.8% M1).
- docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md — US-19.
- docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md — level-2 chain cost re-tune evidence.

# Intake Brief: Ownership-aware AI placement — do not place synergy that only benefits other players

**Work item:** MS-0MUYODDW300690KX · `bug` · `high`
**Discovered from:** observed competitive play — the AI places community spaces that anchor the human player's businesses but give the AI nothing
**Related precedent:** [MS-0MUX8J9KJ005ZKDW](MS-0MUX8J9KJ005ZKDW) (community-space scoring + business-preference penalty), [MS-0MT5X3N79002S038](MS-0MT5X3N79002S038) (competitive ownership-aware AI scoring)

## Headline

In shared-street (competitive) play the AI's placement scoring counts the synergy a card anchors for **every** neighbouring business, regardless of who owns it. A community space that only boosts an opponent's businesses can therefore score positive, and the AI spends coins and pays an ongoing running cost to enrich a rival. The competitive placement score must be ownership-aware: credit only the synergy the acting AI gains, and subtract (or refuse) the synergy it hands to other players, so the AI places a card only when **its own benefit exceeds the benefit it confers on others**.

## Problem statement

`scoreCommunitySpacePlacement` (used by both the single-player and competitive spend chains) computes a community space's value from `neighbourSynergyGain`, which sums the marginal synergy income added to **all** adjacent businesses with no owner filter. In single-player there is only the acting seat, so this is correct. In competitive/shared-street play (`state.ownerTaggedGrid` present, `isCompetitiveMode(state) === true`) the grid holds businesses owned by the acting AI **and** by other seats. When the AI considers a slot adjacent to an opponent's matching-synergy business — but not its own — `neighbourSynergyGain` still returns a positive number, so the community space can clear `COMMUNITY_SPACE_SCORE_PENALTY` and be bought/played. The AI then pays the placement cost and the `ongoingCost × horizon` drain to increase a rival's income.

The same blind spot applies to the other direction for any card: `competitiveBusinessScore` / `competitiveHandBusinessScore` measure only the placed card's own income + synergy and never account for the synergy the placement anchors for neighbouring **opponent** businesses. The seed's general rule — "only place cards (any cards) where the benefits to the AI are greater than to other players" — therefore is not met by the current competitive scoring.

Ownership is already modelled (`getSlotOwnerId` / `ownerTaggedGrid`, `MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`) and used elsewhere in the competitive AI (`countOwnSynergyMatches`, `competitiveUpgradeTargets`), so this is a fix to the scoring path, not a new system.

## Users

- **Human player (seat 0) vs AI opponents** — a shared-street competitive game should not be handed an economic gift by an AI that anchors the human's businesses for free.
  - *"As the human player, I want the AI to compete for its own advantage, so my businesses don't get free synergy the AI paid for."*
- **Producer / game designer** — wants competitive AI behaviour to follow the intended principle (own benefit ≥ benefit to others), with measurable before/after evidence and no change to single-player balance baselines.
  - *"As the producer, I want competitive AI placements to be ownership-aware so the AI plays to win rather than boosting opponents."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Ownership-aware community-space value (competitive).** In competitive mode, `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement` (or a competitive variant invoked by `competitiveBusinessScore` / `competitiveHandBusinessScore`) counts neighbour synergy only for slots owned by the acting player. Synergy anchored for a business owned by any other seat is not credited and is subtracted from the placement score, so the score reflects `own gain − opponent gain`.
2. **Opponent-only community space is rejected.** A community space placed into a slot whose only positive value is synergy for another seat's business scores `≤ 0`; `isCompetitivePlacementEligible` therefore returns `false` and the greedy AI does not buy or play it (measured by a unit test constructing an opponent-owned adjacent business).
3. **Self-beneficial placements preserved.** A community space whose synergy anchors the acting AI's own businesses retains a positive score and is still chosen; a community space anchoring a mix of own and opponent businesses scores strictly less than the identical placement with only own businesses (no regression for genuine self-interest).
4. **All competitive placements charge opponent benefit.** For ordinary business placements in competitive mode, the placement score subtracts the marginal synergy income the placement anchors for neighbouring **opponent** businesses (net differential), while the acting player's own income/synergy valuation is unchanged. The eligibility gate for income-producing businesses is unchanged (they remain always eligible); the differential is reflected in how they rank against alternatives.
5. **Single-player unchanged.** With no `ownerTaggedGrid` (N=1), `scoreAction`, `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement` and `GreedyStrategy` produce identical scores/decisions to today; `tests/main-street/community-space-ai-scoring.test.ts` and `tests/main-street/ai-strategy.test.ts` pass unmodified.
6. **Determinism preserved.** The same seed + same strategy yields an identical competitive action sequence (`CompetitiveGreedyStrategy`), and no RNG is introduced into the ownership-aware scoring.
7. **Evidence captured.** Before/after competitive head-to-head evidence shows the rate of placements conferring net benefit on opponents falls (net of single-player baselines, which are unchanged), committed alongside the change.
8. **Documentation updated.** The competitive placement rule (own benefit must exceed benefit handed to other seats) is documented in the AI strategy docs and code doc-comments, including the `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement` / competitive-score comments.
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Scoring heuristic only — no engine or rule changes.** Reuse the existing ownership model (`getSlotOwnerId`, `ownerTaggedGrid`) and the existing synergy computation (`computeSynergyBonus`); do not change income routing, `computeSynergyBonus` semantics, or the same-type penalty.
- **Single-player paths must remain behaviourally identical** (N=1 fallback), preserving the committed Monte Carlo balance baselines (`docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json`).
- **Preserve the existing business-preference semantics** (`COMMUNITY_SPACE_SCORE_PENALTY`, positive-score eligibility for community spaces).
- **No new randomness;** scoring stays deterministic.
- **Reputation and shared/global effects** stay valued as they are today (reputation is per-owner; only synergy-attribution changes).
- **Scope-creep risk:** widening this into a full multi-seat minimax/opponent-modelling rework, or retuning card costs, is out of scope — record follow-ups as linked work items.

## Existing state

- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `neighbourSynergyGain(grid, placed, slotIndex, bonusPerNeighbor)` sums synergy gains for every neighbour with no owner filter (lines ~180–206). `communitySpacePlacementValueAt` uses it for `neighbourIncome`; `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement` is the public entry point and is called from `competitiveBusinessScore` / `competitiveHandBusinessScore` (the "competitive mirror" explicitly documented in `docs/main-street/community-space-ai-evidence.md`). `competitiveBusinessScore` / `competitiveHandBusinessScore` for ordinary businesses count only `(baseIncome + projectedSynergy) × horizon − cost`. `isCompetitivePlacementEligible` gates community spaces on `score > 0`.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts` — `getSlotOwnerId(state, slotIndex)` (owner tag with active-player fallback) and `ownerTaggedGrid`; the established ownership source used by `countOwnSynergyMatches` and `competitiveUpgradeTargets`.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — `computeSynergyBonus(grid, index, bonusPerNeighbor, soldSlots, gridDims)`; the ownership-agnostic per-card synergy used by the before/after diff.
- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — competitive head-to-head harness (`runCompetitiveMonteCarlo`, `CompetitiveGreedyStrategy`) for before/after evidence.
- Existing competitive scoring is already ownership-aware for events (`computeCompetitiveEventValue` counts only the acting player's matching businesses) and upgrades (own slots only); placement is the remaining ownership-blind path.
- Tests: `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts` (ownership-aware scoring, `place()` fixture tagging owners), `tests/main-street/community-space-ai-scoring.test.ts` (single-player community-space value), `tests/main-street/no-phantom-synergy.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/same-type-synergy.test.ts`.

## Desired change

1. Introduce an ownership-aware neighbour-synergy attribution helper (e.g. `neighbourSynergyGainByOwner(...)` returning `{ own, opponent }`, or an optional owner filter on `neighbourSynergyGain`), using `getSlotOwnerId(state, i)` against the acting seat.
2. Use it in the competitive placement value so a community space's `neighbourIncome` credits only the acting player's slots and subtracts (or excludes and negatively weights) opponent slots, yielding an `own − opponent` net placement value.
3. Apply the same opponent-benefit term to the ordinary business competitive scores so any placement is penalised by the synergy it anchors for opponents.
4. Keep single-player `scoreAction` / `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement` on the ownership-agnostic path (all slots belong to the acting seat) so baselines do not move.
5. Add focused unit tests (own-only, opponent-only, mixed) and capture before/after competitive Monte Carlo evidence; update the AI strategy docs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — add ownership-aware neighbour-synergy attribution; thread it through `communitySpacePlacementValueAt` / `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement` and `competitiveBusinessScore` / `competitiveHandBusinessScore`; keep `isCompetitivePlacementEligible` gating community spaces on the ownership-aware score.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts` — reference only (`getSlotOwnerId`, `ownerTaggedGrid`); no change expected.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — reference only (`computeSynergyBonus`); no change expected.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts` — new AC1–AC3 tests: opponent-owned adjacent business makes an opponent-only community space ineligible; own-only placement stays positive; mixed placement scores below own-only.
- `tests/main-street/community-space-ai-scoring.test.ts` — confirm single-player scores are unchanged (AC5).
- `tests/main-street/ai-strategy.test.ts` — confirm `GreedyStrategy` decisions unchanged (AC5).
- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — reference for the competitive harness; add/extend a report to capture opponent-benefit placement rate if needed.
- `src/scripts/balance/community-space-placement-report.ts` — reference/extension point for before/after evidence.
- `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md` — document the competitive ownership-aware placement rule (own benefit must exceed opponent benefit).
- `docs/main-street/community-space-ai-evidence.md` — note that the competitive mirror is now ownership-aware.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUX8J9KJ005ZKDW** (completed) — *AI uses community space cards too much.* Introduced `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement`, the neighbour-anchoring value and `COMMUNITY_SPACE_SCORE_PENALTY`; this item fixes the ownership blind spot left in that competitive mirror.
- **MS-0MT5X3N79002S038** (completed) — *Competitive AI strategy: ownership-aware, staff-free scoring for shared-street play.* Established the competitive scoring/enumeration layer this change extends; its AC1 ("ownership-aware scoring") currently covers resources/own businesses but not the synergy handed to opponents.
- **MS-0MTIIL6J200291ZQ** (completed) — *Per-owner income routing; shared event/incident resolution.* Established per-owner income accrual on the shared street (why opponent synergy gain is a real benefit to a rival).
- **MS-0MUVB2ZES005V83Y** (completed) — *AI should not use Community Favour as much.* Same family of AI-heuristic corrections.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (from seed):** the target is competitive/shared-street play ("other players"); single-player has no opponent and must not change.
- **Assumption (from seed):** the general principle applies to *any* card, so ordinary business placements also subtract opponent benefit; the observed, most damaging case is community spaces.
- **Assumption:** "benefit to other players" from a placement means the marginal synergy income credited to their businesses; reputation/global events are out of scope (valued as today).
- **Balance risk:** subtracting opponent benefit could suppress legitimate business placements in tight shared-street configurations. Mitigation: keep own income/base value intact and subtract only the anchored opponent synergy; verify against the competitive harness that AI scores/win rate do not regress materially.
- **Baseline risk:** touching a shared helper could leak into single-player. Mitigation: explicit N=1 fallback and unchanged single-player tests (`community-space-ai-scoring.test.ts`, `ai-strategy.test.ts`, Monte Carlo baseline guardrail).
- **Determinism risk:** adding ownership lookups must not introduce ordering/RNG variance. Mitigation: AC6 determinism test.
- **Scope-creep risk:** a full opponent-modelling/minimax rewrite, or cost retuning, is out of scope — record extra opportunities as linked work items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope — which seats):** "Is this competitive (multi-seat shared-street) only, or also single-player?" — Answer (agent, research-driven): "Competitive only. The seed says 'the player' and 'other players', and single-player has no opponent; `isCompetitiveMode` and `ownerTaggedGrid` already distinguish the two. Single-player behaviour must remain identical." Source: self-research of `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` (`isCompetitiveMode`, `getSlotOwnerId`) and `docs/main-street/community-space-ai-evidence.md`. Accepted: competitive-only change with N=1 fallback.
- **Q2 (scope — card families):** "Which placements must be ownership-aware — community spaces only, or all cards?" — Answer (agent, research-driven): "All cards, per the seed's 'any cards'. The scoring change is generalised, but community spaces are the observed defect and the primary acceptance test; ordinary businesses keep their own income and are penalised only by the opponent synergy they anchor." Source: seed description; `competitiveBusinessScore` / `competitiveHandBusinessScore` inspection. Accepted.
- **Q3 (objective function):** "Is the AI objective 'ignore opponent benefit' or 'maximise own benefit − opponent benefit'?" — Answer (agent, research-driven): "'Own benefit − opponent benefit', per 'benefits to the AI are greater than to other players'. A placement that helps an opponent more than the AI should score ≤ 0 and be rejected for community spaces." Source: seed description; existing `isCompetitivePlacementEligible` `score > 0` gate. Accepted.
- **Q4 (verification):** "What proves the fix?" — Answer (agent, research-driven): "Focused unit tests (own-only positive, opponent-only rejected, mixed scores below own-only) plus before/after competitive Monte Carlo evidence and the unchanged single-player suite/baselines." Source: `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts` fixtures; `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`. Accepted.
- **No producer-blocking open questions.** The seed plus existing ownership infrastructure make the intent clear; assumptions above are recorded for producer confirmation at the review gate.

- **MS-0MUOSUMNK000QZ62** – Update documentation for Investor card and mechanics (blocked)
- **MS-0MUV9P89G0061SRA** – Prevent players from selling, closing, or upgrading businesses they do not own (open)

# Add ownership-aware placement scoring tests

**Work item:** Parent AC1–AC6 (test coverage) — test-first, expected red until the implementation lands.
**Parent:** MS-0MUYODDW300690KX (AI should not place synergies that only benefit the player)

## Summary

Add focused unit tests that pin the ownership-aware competitive placement contract **before** the implementation lands (test-first). The tests construct competitor-owned adjacent businesses using the existing owner-tagging fixture (`place(...)`) and assert the `own − opponent` net placement value, the community-space eligibility gate, and that single-player scoring is untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Opponent-only community space is rejected.** With an adjacent business owned by another seat, `scoreCommunitySpacePlacement(...)` returns `<= 0` and `CompetitiveGreedyStrategy` does not buy or play the card.
- **Self-beneficial placement preserved.** A community space whose synergy anchors the acting AI's own adjacent business still scores `> 0` and is selected.
- **Mixed placement is discounted.** A community space anchoring a mix of own and opponent businesses scores strictly less than the identical placement adjacent to only own businesses.
- **Ordinary business differential.** In competitive mode, an ordinary business placement's score is reduced by the marginal synergy it anchors for neighbouring opponent businesses; the acting player's own income/synergy valuation is unchanged and the action remains eligible.
- **Single-player unchanged.** `tests/main-street/community-space-ai-scoring.test.ts` and `tests/main-street/ai-strategy.test.ts` pass unmodified (no `ownerTaggedGrid`, N=1).
- **Determinism.** Same seed + `CompetitiveGreedyStrategy` yields an identical competitive action sequence.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Extend `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts` with a community-space fixture and an owner-tagged neighbour setup.
2. Add own-only, opponent-only and mixed scoring cases.
3. Add the ordinary-business opponent-benefit differential case.
4. Add the N=1 single-player regression assertion and a competitive determinism test.

## Dependencies

- None (test-first; runs red until the implementation item lands).

## Deliverables

- New/updated unit tests covering parent AC1–AC6.

**Key Files:**
- `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/community-space-ai-scoring.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/ai-strategy.test.ts`
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`

# Slice 1: Effective-threshold helper and competitive win check

**Parent:** MS-0MUZH6V7C0091SGE (Competitive mode: divide the score target by the number of players) · slice 1 of 4
**Test-first:** write the failing Vitest cases below **before** adding the helper.

## Goal

Introduce the single source of truth for the competitive win target and make the competitive
win check use it, so a game with `P` seats (human + AI) is won at
`Math.round(baseWinThreshold / P / 50) * 50`.

Worked values (base → effective): Easy 10000 → P=2 5000, P=3 3350, P=4 2500;
Medium 12000 → 6000 / 4000 / 3000; Hard 15000 → 7500 / 5000 / 3750.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (parent AC1).** In a competitive game with `P` players (`state.playerCount`, human + AI) the win check threshold equals `roundToNearest50(baseWinThreshold / P)` — `Math.round(baseWinThreshold / P / 50) * 50` — and the first seat whose per-owner score reaches it is declared `competitiveWinnerId`. Slice tests pin Easy P=2 5000, P=3 3350, P=4 2500 and are written red before the helper exists.
- **AC2 (parent AC1).** In a competitive game with `P` players (`state.playerCount`, human + AI) the win check threshold equals `roundToNearest50(baseWinThreshold / P)` — `Math.round(baseWinThreshold / P / 50) * 50` — and the first seat whose per-owner score reaches it is declared `competitiveWinnerId`. A single pure `effectiveWinThreshold(state)` returns `Math.round(state.config.winThreshold / (state.playerCount ?? 1) / 50) * 50`, and no other site in `src/` duplicates the division.
- **AC3 (parent AC1).** In a competitive game with `P` players (`state.playerCount`, human + AI) the win check threshold equals `roundToNearest50(baseWinThreshold / P)` — `Math.round(baseWinThreshold / P / 50) * 50` — and the first seat whose per-owner score reaches it is declared `competitiveWinnerId`. The competitive win check compares each per-owner score against the effective win threshold for P = 2, 3, 4 and declares that seat `competitiveWinnerId` with `endReason = 'score_threshold'`.
- **AC4 (parent AC3).** Single-player (no `players[]` / `playerCount` undefined) continues to use the base `winThreshold`, which is already a multiple of 50 so the rounding is a no-op. The competitive entry point delegates to `checkEndConditions` and an explicit assertion pins the unchanged base value.
- **AC5 (parent AC5).** A resumed competitive game re-derives the effective win threshold from the persisted `playerCount`; no stale threshold survives a load. A serialise then deserialise round-trip of a P=3 Easy state re-derives 3350; a legacy save with no `playerCount` yields the base threshold.
- **AC6 (parent AC6).** New Vitest coverage for AC1–AC5 (engine, AI, UI strings, serialisation) and the full project test suite passes; the new tests fail against the pre-change code. (this slice: helper, competitive win check, persistence guards).
- **AC7.** The endless-mode branch uses the effective win threshold and keeps `endReason = 'score_threshold_continue'` and its idempotent re-entry behaviour unchanged.

*Metric:* unit tests for AC1–AC4 red then green; source grep for AC2; regression-guard test for AC5; `npm test` for AC6 and AC7.
## Minimal implementation

- Add `effectiveWinThreshold(state)` to `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` with a doc comment
  stating the competitive `base / playerCount`, nearest-50 rule and the single-player no-op.
- Re-export it from `src/MainStreetState.ts` if consumers import through the barrel.
- Replace `state.config.winThreshold` with the helper in `checkCompetitiveEndConditions`
  (both the standard and endless branches) in `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`; leave
  `checkEndConditions` untouched.
- Add the round-trip and legacy-save guards to the competitive save/load suite.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`
- `src/MainStreetState.ts`
- `tests/main-street/competitive-end-condition-ai-win.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/competitive-save-load.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- None. This slice is the prerequisite for slices 2–4.
- Note: MS-0MUXLP6V00075IQY (Fix win/loss attribution in `checkCompetitiveEndConditions`,
  blocked) touches the same function — rebase on it if it lands first.

## Deliverables

- `effectiveWinThreshold` helper with unit coverage.
- Competitive win check (standard + endless) routed through the helper.
- Persistence regression guards.
